question: Can a bounded counter-driven mean-reverting log2 exposure trajectory provide exact temporal flicker state handoff while avoiding the frame-to-frame jumps of an iid gamma control and the drift of a random walk?

primary_source.title: AbsoluteDegradation: A Physics-Inspired Synthetic Film-Degradation Pipeline and Archival Film Restoration Benchmark
primary_source.use: latest film-degradation baseline and exact per-frame iid gamma control from equation text; the candidate is a clean-room bounded exposure-domain alternative
excluded: claim that iid gamma is physically calibrated flicker

forbidden: claim the synthetic profile is measured from a film camera, projector, scanner or stock
apply flicker after density, scanner or output transform
use per-frame gamma as the candidate physical exposure operator
add spatial banding, rolling-shutter, color drift or automatic exposure compensation
change profile, controls, gates or seed after formal scoring

branch_rule.pass: retain the typed deterministic temporal exposure primitive as an independently switchable synthetic reference and next test composition order with development response
branch_rule.fail: close this exact temporal exposure mechanism without parameter or threshold rescue

claim_ceiling: Synthetic deterministic exposure-domain flicker mechanism only; not measured film-camera exposure variance, projector flicker, scanner instability, temporal video quality, product readiness or stock calibration.
